title: Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake: How Blockchains Agree (Beginner Guide)
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Proof of work vs proof of stake in plain English. Sources: ethereum.org, CBC, FXStreet. AI-generated voice.

scenes.head: WHO KEEPS IT HONEST?
scenes.narration: A blockchain has no boss. So how does everyone agree on which transactions are real?

scenes.head: PROOF OF WORK
items: Computers race to solve a puzzle
scenes.narration: Bitcoin uses proof of work. Computers race to solve a puzzle, and the winner adds the next block.

scenes.head: THE COST IS THE POINT
scenes.narration: The energy cost makes cheating expensive. But it also means the network uses a lot of power.

scenes.head: PROOF OF STAKE
scenes.narration: Proof of stake works differently. Validators lock up their own coins, and dishonest ones can lose them.

scenes.head: ETHEREUM SWITCHED
scenes.narration: Ethereum switched to proof of stake in September twenty twenty two. Reports say it cut its energy use by about ninety nine percent.

scenes.head: TRADE OFFS
scenes.narration: Both systems are widely used, and each has critics. They simply make different trade offs.
